title: Wrap words into lines
description: Break a text into lines of at most a given width. The words are the space-separated words of the text; empty pieces from extra spaces are not words. Fill the lines greedily from the first word: a word goes onto the current line, with one space before it, if the line then stays within the width; otherwise it starts a new line. A word that is longer than the width stands alone on its own line without being cut. Join the lines with a vertical bar "|". A text without words gives the empty text. A width below 1 is an error with the message "width must be positive", even for an empty text.
notes: A line of exactly the width is allowed (<=, not <); an over-long word still opens a fresh line for the next word; the width check precedes everything.
